concerns.text: Phase 0.5 (Spec Resolution) tasks T054-T059 are listed as pending, yet Phase 2 (Foundational) task T019 is marked [X] (completed). T019 implements 'MP_API_KEY' configuration, which contradicts the current spec assumption ('no authentication barriers') that T056 is supposed to fix. Implementation of T019 occurred before the spec dependency (T056) was resolved, violating the 'Producer before Consumer' rule where the Spec is the producer of requirements for the code.

Task T020 (Test Set Partitioning) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) and placed before T025 (Filtering). However, T025 explicitly states it must exclude indices in 'data/processed/test_set_indices.csv' (output of T020). If T025 runs before T020 completes, it will fail or include test data in training. Marking T020 as [P] implies it has no dependencies, but T025 and T031 are consumers of T020's artifact. The [P] tag is incorrect for T020 in the context of the US1 block execution flow, or the dependency on T020 for T025/T031 is missing.

Task T032 (K-Means clustering to generate 7 subsets) is marked [X] (completed) but depends on T031 (RSS capping). T031 is also marked [X]. However, T031's description says it reads from 'data/processed/filtered_pool.csv' (output of T025). T025 is marked [ ] (pending). The dependency chain T025 -> T031 -> T032 is broken in the status markers: downstream tasks (T031, T032) are marked complete while their upstream producer (T025) is pending. This violates the 'Foundational tasks first' and 'Producer before consumer' ordering.

Task T020 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). While it has no upstream dependencies, it is a strict prerequisite for T025 and T031. The [P] tag suggests it can run in parallel with other US1 tasks, but T025 and T031 cannot start until T020 finishes. The tag is technically correct for T020 itself (it doesn't wait), but the visual grouping implies T020, T025, and T031 are parallel peers, which is misleading for the execution order.
